The design gate

An optional check on every pick: does this goal carry a confirmed design? When the gate is on, a goal without one is not worked. It is set aside and a design ticket is filed. The gate is off by default.

On this page
  • What the gate does
  • The label
  • A goal without the label
  • On or off
  • How the retrofit works
  • A design here means: someone mapped the goal onto the real code, listed what it touches and what is still unsure, and a second pass confirmed it.
  • A confirmed design leaves a mark on the goal: the label sdlc:designed.
  • Goals that come through the idea front end get the mark automatically once confirmed. Goals you file by hand do not.
  • The gate is for the second kind. With it on, a hand-filed goal is stopped, a design ticket is filed for it, and the loop moves on to the next goal.
  • With the gate off, which is the default, nothing is stopped and goals run exactly as before.
Read before switching it on

Turning the gate on applies to the whole live backlog. Every open goal without the label is parked on its next pick, each with its own design ticket. That is a decision, not just a setting.

What the gate does

The gate parks and files; it never designs the goal itself. The design ticket is ordinary work for the loop or for you.

The label

QuestionAnswer
Namesdlc:designed
What it meansThe goal was designed and the design was independently confirmed
Who writes itOnly the confirmation step, /sigma-goal-review, and only on a confirmation
Who reads itOnly the gate
Kind of labelAn overlay: it rides alongside the goal's lifecycle state and does not replace it. See Labels
Removed byNothing. No step clears it

A goal without the label

GateGoal has the labelGoal lacks the label
Off (default)WorkedWorked
OnWorkedParked, a design ticket filed, the next goal taken

Two kinds of ticket are exempt because they are bookkeeping: the design tickets the gate files itself, and the tickets filed to split an oversized goal. A child created by splitting is not exempt; it gets its own check.

On or off

The gate is off in a fresh setup. To turn it on, set this in .sdlc/config.json:

"goal_design": { "enabled": true, "mode": "full" }
  • enabled must be exactly true. Absent, false or anything else means off.
  • mode is the depth of the design pass written into the ticket: full (the default) or lane. It never changes whether the gate acts; once enabled it always parks and files. An unrecognised value falls back to lane with a warning.

The idea front end does not depend on the gate. It runs whether the gate is on or off.

How the retrofit works

Retrofit is the gate's job: making sure goals that did not come through the front end are mapped onto the code before they are built.

  1. The gate parks the goal

    On the goal's next pick it finds no label, files one design ticket titled with the goal's number and title, and leaves a marker comment on the goal so it is never filed twice.

  2. The design ticket is worked

    It is picked like any goal. Its instructions say to design the target goal, not the ticket, and to write no code.

  3. Goal Review confirms or rejects

    A confirmation adds sdlc:designed to the target goal. A rejection writes one comment and nothing else.

  4. A person restores the goal

    /sigma-unpark puts the goal back in the backlog. Confirming a design does not do this by itself.

Technical detail

The three results

ResultMeaningThe loop
OFFThe gate is not enabledCarries on
PROCEEDAlready designed, or exemptCarries on
PARKED <reason>Not designed; a design ticket was filed, or filing could not be confirmed safeDoes not research it, takes the next goal

Where it sits and how it fails

  • Order. After the duplicate and oversized checks, before readiness and model selection.
  • Fail-open early, fail-closed late. A transient failure before the label is read proceeds, so the gate cannot freeze the loop. Once the label read has been attempted, a failure or a malformed answer parks, because an unreadable label set must never be treated as designed.
  • Local backlog. A source with no issue tracker can neither confirm "not designed" nor file a ticket, so it parks with the reason that the check needs an issue tracker.
  • Idempotency. A marker comment on the goal means a second pick files nothing and parks with a pointer to the comments.
  • Ticket assignment. If the design ticket could not be assigned, no loop can see it until a person assigns it. The park detail says so.
  • Reconcile first. The ticket tells its worker to stop if the target is already closed or designed, and, when two design tickets exist for one target, to defer to the lower-numbered one.

Limits, stated

  • The gate reads one fact: whether the label is present. It does not check that a design file exists or is still current.
  • The label write is best-effort. If it fails, nothing retries and nothing sweeps for a confirmed design without its label.
  • A rejection is a single comment. Nothing re-runs the design automatically.
  • Where the confirmation skill is not installed, a person applies the label by hand once a design is confirmed.
  • Turning the gate on parks the whole undesigned backlog on its next pick. Whether that suits a given backlog was not measured.

The contract is the dossier pipeline document; the labels are in Labels.
